name: Barak
bio:
Barak was the son of Abinoam, of the tribe of Naphtali, summoned by the prophetess Deborah to lead Israel under the LORD's command and defeat Sisera, commander of the Canaanite army, whose nine hundred iron chariots had oppressed Israel for twenty years.

Deborah relayed the LORD's command for Barak to take ten thousand men of Naphtali and Zebulun to Mount Tabor to confront Sisera; Barak told her, "If you go with me, I will go; but if you don't go with me, I won't go," and Deborah agreed to go with him, though she also prophesied the honor of the victory would belong to a woman (Judges 4:6-9). In the battle, the LORD routed Sisera's entire army before Barak, who pursued them to total destruction, while Sisera himself abandoned his chariot and fled on foot, only to be killed later by Jael (Judges 4:10-16).

After the victory, Barak joined Deborah in singing the triumphant song recorded in Judges 5, celebrating the LORD's mighty acts for Israel. The New Testament book of Hebrews lists Barak among the heroes who accomplished great things "by faith," alongside Gideon, Samson, and David (Hebrews 11:32) — showing that although he initially hesitated and asked Deborah to accompany him, he ultimately carried out by faith the deliverance the LORD had entrusted to him.
